title: Automatic module cache cleanup
objective: Run conservative bounded module-cache pruning automatically off the startup path while preserving manual prune semantics, active leases, current, pinned, and recent compiler versions

oracles: manual prune policy and temporary-cache fixtures

handoff.summary: Automatic versioned-module-cache maintenance is scheduled through the existing process lease path. Startup performs only exact-path metadata checks and reads one small state marker, then an unreferenced timer launches an unreferenced detached worker. The worker uses the existing conservative prune policy, preserves current/newest/recent/pinned/leased versions, serializes passes with a stale-safe lock, records its last attempt, and caps both attempted bytes and attempted versions per pass. Manual cache-prune plan, output, dry-run, and application semantics are unchanged. The test manifest also now includes two previously landed tests and removes one duplicate entry.
risks: Automatic retention settings are environment variables rather than public CLI flags; invalid settings fail closed and the manual prune command remains the diagnostic path.

The full integration tier had 14 unrelated worktree-environment failures because only the FLINT native package was prepared; missing FFLAS, graph, M4RI, and production-kernel artifacts caused 13, while one dense-prime timing ratchet failed under concurrent load. The complete root integration suite was independently green immediately before this lane's final validation.
